note.explanation: A binary ionic compound is made from two ions: a cation and an anion. Write their symbols and charges, crisscross the charge numbers to become subscripts, and drop the charge signs. The resulting compound must be electrically neutral.
examples: Magnesium nitride: Mg²⁺ and N³⁻ give Mg₃N₂.
Aluminium oxide: Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃.
note.simple: Balance the positive and negative charges by crossing the charge numbers down as subscripts.
note.checkQuestion: What is the formula of barium nitride?
note.title: Writing formulas of binary ionic compounds
steps: Write the symbol and charge of the cation, then the symbol and charge of the anion.
Cross the numerical charge values to become the other ion's subscripts.
Drop the charge signs and write the formula.
note.answer: Use the ion charges as crossed subscripts to write an electrically neutral formula.

mcqs.stem: What is the chemical formula of sodium chloride?
rationales: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ balance in a one-to-one ratio, so NaCl is correct.
Na₂Cl has an overall positive charge and is not neutral.
NaCl₂ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.
Na₂Cl₂ is not written in the simplest ratio; it reduces to NaCl.

mcqs.stem: Which formula is formed by Ca²⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: The charges balance in a one-to-one ratio, giving CaO.
Ca₂O has a net positive charge and is not neutral.
CaO₂ has a net negative charge and is not neutral.
Ca₂O₃ does not balance the stated ion charges.

mcqs.stem: What is the formula of the compound formed from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: AlO does not balance the +3 and −2 charges.
AlO₃ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.
Crisscrossing the charge numbers gives Al₂O₃, which is neutral.
Al₃O₂ does not balance the stated ion charges.

mcqs.stem: Which is the formula of magnesium nitride, formed from Mg²⁺ and N³⁻?
rationales: MgN does not balance the +2 and −3 charges.
Mg₂N₃ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.
Crisscrossing the charge numbers gives Mg₃N₂, which is neutral.
MgN₂ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.

mcqs.stem: What is the formula of lithium oxide, formed from Li⁺ and O²⁻?
rationales: LiO does not balance the +1 and −2 charges.
Two Li⁺ ions balance one O²⁻ ion, so Li₂O is correct.
LiO₂ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.
Li₂O₂ is not written in the simplest ratio; it reduces to Li₂O.

mcqs.stem: What is the formula of barium nitride, formed from Ba²⁺ and N³⁻?
rationales: BaN does not balance the +2 and −3 charges.
Ba₂N₃ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.
Three Ba²⁺ ions and two N³⁻ ions balance, giving Ba₃N₂.
BaN₂ has an overall negative charge and is not neutral.

examTips: A board question may ask you to write the formula from the compound's name or from the ion symbols and charges.
For a short formula question, show the ion charges and the crisscross step as well as the final formula; this can earn method marks.
Check that the final numbers of positive and negative charges balance, and write the charge numbers as subscripts without their signs.

example.question: Write down the formula of Magnesium nitride.

explain.title: Start with the two ions
explain.body: In order to write down the formula of an ionic compound, first identify the cations and anions and the number of charges present on them. Finally combine the two ions together to form an electrically neutral compound.

explain.title: Use the ion charges
explain.body: Write the symbol of the cation with its charge, then the symbol of the anion with its charge. The charges tell you how many of each ion are needed for a neutral compound.

explain.title: Apply the crisscross method
explain.body: In this method, the numerical value of each of the ion charges is crossed over to become the subscript of the other ion. Signs of the charges are then dropped.

explain.title: Check the result
explain.body: The compound must be electrically neutral. For Mg₃N₂, three Mg²⁺ ions give +6 and two N³⁻ ions give −6, so the charges balance.

mistakes: Leaving the charge signs in the final formula instead of dropping them.
Putting each charge number on the same ion instead of crisscrossing it to the other ion.
Writing a formula that does not have equal total positive and negative charges.
Forgetting that a subscript of 1 is not written.
